value: Geology and Mineral Resources of Nigeria - combined, EPSG:4326
WGS 84, longitude/latitude, EPSG:4326, degrees
NGSA Geological Map of Nigeria, 1:2,000,000 (2011 edition, DG Prof. Siyan Malomo); vector PDF, 125 layers
NGSA Mineral Resources Map of Nigeria, 1:2,000,000, 2nd edition 2023 (DG Dr Abdulrazaq Garba); vector PDF
affine fitted to printed 1-degree graticule: lon = (x + 276.36)/157.593, lat = (2281.63 - y)/157.586; residual 0.20 pt

the 2023 sheet's own printed graticule gives lon = (x + 288.95)/157.5987, lat = (2572.35 - y)/157.6015 (residual 0.000 pt). The affine the extraction stored - lon = (x + 288.67)/157.288, lat = (2575.87 - y)/157.602 - is 0.2 % out in longitude scale and 3.5 pt out in latitude offset, which is why the mineral_symbols and mineral_localities positions are withdrawn: see mineral_audit.md. The measured graticule is what minerals_named uses
Both sheets are unprojected equirectangular at 157.6 pt/deg = 1:2,000,000; datum treated as WGS 84 (Minna datum would shift ~100-200 m, below drawing resolution)
1 pt = 0.7 km on the ground; graticule fit <0.3 pt; residual cartographic disagreement between the two sheets ~5 km median, 20 km p90

geology_units sums to 907,157 km2, which is the national_territory polygon exactly (0.000 % between EPSG:4326, EPSG:6933 and the geodesic computation). The official land area is 923,768 km2, 1.7 % larger: the official figure treats Lake Chad and the coastal creeks differently, so it is not a check on this layer - the territory polygon is what the geology was cut on
No attribute tables exist in either PDF; codes, strata and ages were reconstructed from layer names, the printed legend and in-polygon labels

fetch_source.py -> build_combined.py (18 base layers) -> build_geology_final.py (the geology layer) -> refine_localities.py -> anchor_to_icons.py -> finalize_layers.py -> render_combined.py -> audit_layers.py

the PDF's own paint order (src_seq, preserved for all 1,518 paths) decides every overlap: a path loses exactly the part covered by any path drawn after it. Checked against the printed ink: 1,426 of 1,462 polygons carry their own colour at a sample point (97.5%). That is a one-sample-per-polygon test, not an area-weighted one - see README 'How faithful is the geology layer'

the 2011 legend has 92 rows but 87 codes: Esh, MS, MyP, Ncsh and Wss are printed twice, each row a different rock; units are resolved per legend row. Printed codes Glls and OGe were normalised onto legend rows GIls (same printed colour, Dukamaje Formation) and OGp (same rock, colour and era). Five printed units are absent from the legend (OGp, Gdss, Gmsh, LCM, S) and flagged attr_source = in-map label

the 2011 sheet draws neighbouring-country context: 16.9% of the rivers' length, 7.5% of roads, 7.8% of state boundaries and 23 of 486 towns lie outside the border. Kept and flagged per feature (frac_in_nigeria on lines, in_nigeria on points)

one layer only: geology_units = the 1,518 paths of the 2011 sheet replayed in the order the PDF paints them, clipped to national_territory, every inland gap filled (97 rows = 96 rock units + W water; 0.002 km2 residual overlap, 0.0 km2 uncovered, ink agreement 97.5%)
national_territory = international_boundary (2023, land border only, 3,500 vertices) spliced into the Natural Earth 10m Nigeria coastline (public domain)

1,323 printed mineral symbols re-detected on the sheet at its native 75 dpi, each point the centroid of its glyph; named against the source extraction's appearance reference with 80.8% leave-one-out accuracy, per-row tier probable/tentative/unidentified. Positions are valid; per-mineral totals are not (Limestone 30 vs 136) - use mineral_symbols.mineral for counts - filtered on is_symbol = 1, see mineral_symbols_note - and this layer for position. 144 symbols sit outside the border because the sheet maps the whole region; in_nigeria flags them. See mineral_audit.md and minerals_named.md

audit_layers.py verified all 31 feature layers, 9 rasters and the file's own registers (dangling gpkg_extensions rows, orphan and undeclared spatial indexes, empty tile-matrix zoom levels, blank descriptions): 0 problems, area 907,157 km2 identical to +0.000% between EPSG:4326 / 6933 / geodesic, 2023 border within 7.5 m of the geology edge, 0 point-to-unit join mismatches

1,609 rows, of which 1,489 are countable printed symbols: is_symbol = 0 marks 56 raster slivers, 21 state-capital squares, 8 linework/label fragments, 5 bridge or water markings, 5 merged clusters, 15 fragments and 8 halves of a symbol already counted, and 2 merged touching pairs. Filter on is_symbol before counting a commodity. The positions in this layer are withdrawn (median 9.6 km from any printed symbol); minerals_named carries the valid positions

5 units have no era on the sheet (Gdss, s, P, Gmsh, BCT: 5,296 km2, 0.6 % of the layer) because they are printed labels with no legend row, or a legend row that leaves the era blank. Their stratigraphic fields are NULL - not guessed - and they are listed in geology_final_report.json -> units_without_era. The PNG's era legend carries them as their own entry

a unit that ends up with no area is dropped from geology_units and recorded in geology_final_report.json -> units_dropped_no_area with the reason. Ts (legend row 34) is dropped that way: the sheet prints it under Qs, so the paint-order replay leaves it no area

31 layers: 26 in EPSG:4326 (57,364 features), 3 in EPSG:32632 (2,095), 2 in EPSG:6933 (1,096). Storage CRS is 4326; the projected copies exist so that area and length never have to be computed in degrees.
31 feature layers, 60,555 features, plus 9 georeferenced raster layers

GeoNames allCountries dump, 2014-10-02 build (CC BY 4.0, attribution 'GeoNames, geonames.org'), via github.com/albert-decatur/geonames2sqlite@1515c01, joined to Natural Earth admin-1 states (public domain, nvkelso/natural-earth-vector@ca96624) for the state name

45,415 populated places, EPSG:4326, built by build_towns.py. 98.9% inside national_territory (the 500 outside are a median 0.8 km beyond the border, generalisation); 15 major cities agree with published coordinates to 0.55 km median; 99.8% carry a state; 450 carry a population figure. Kept beside the 486 printed 2011 labels (layer 'towns') rather than replacing them. See towns_geonames.md

9 georeferenced scanned maps (DEM, soil pH, temperature, forest reserves, land cover, population, ethnic groups, dominant soils, general geology) as clipped RGBA tiles in EPSG:4326, built by georef_new_map.py. Mean border offset 5.7 km, mean overlap 0.941. See RASTER_LAYERS.md

raster-or-vector was decided per sheet by measurement (RASTER_VS_VECTOR.md): poly_soil_ph (111 polygons, 5 pH classes, 906,612 km2, 99.94% of the territory covered) and poly_population (299 polygons, 5 classes, 839,255 km2, 92.51% - the rest is blank on the sheet and is left blank) are traced from the sheets, clipped to the border, with the palette measured from the printed legend swatches and the class polygons re-tested against the sheet (polygon_colour_check.json: 100% / 99.3% within dE 24 at polygon interior points); soil-pH ink seams no wider than 3 px are repaired, population's blank areas are not, because 66.9% of them lie more than 12 px from any fill. The soil sheet's first swatch is printed dark navy with no readable value and is kept as 'unlabelled (dark navy, legend swatch 1)', not guessed as '0'. geology_era (7 eras) is dissolved from the attributed geology_units rather than traced from a 2.5 km/px screenshot; the other six sheets stay rasters because they are rendered surfaces (hillshade, isotherms, dotted fills) or too coarse to gain anything.

the colour-to-class legend in the old IMAGES table was transcribed by eye and was up to dE 100 wrong (median 15-27). read_legend_swatches.py measures the printed swatches off each sheet; those measured colours are what the polygon layers carry in legend_hex

the file's self-description was audited and repaired (fix_gpkg_hygiene.py, gpkg_hygiene_before.json -> gpkg_hygiene.json): 16 gpkg_extensions rows named things that do not exist (7 dropped exploratory layers, 9 rtree declarations on raster tile_data BLOBs), 7 orphan rtree indexes removed, 17 spatial indexes that existed but were undeclared are now declared (every feature layer has exactly one), and 29 of 38 declared tile-matrix zoom levels held no tiles and were dropped - each raster now declares exactly the one level that holds tiles. All 40 layers now carry a gpkg_contents description (describe_layers.py), which audit_layers.py checks.

Missing values are NULL, never '' - enforced, not hoped for: normalise_nulls.py rewrites any empty string to NULL and audit_layers.py fails if one reappears (131,755 cells across 9 layers were normalised on 2026-10-27). Booleans are stored as BOOLEAN 1/0 (never 'True' text), counts and elevations as INTEGER (never numeric text). Every projected copy is attribute-identical to the layer it copies; before this pass the copies disagreed (NULL became '' on a read/write round trip). lon/lat and the geometry are the same point in every point layer.

A layer-by-layer audit on 2026-10-27 checked every one of the 31 layers against its own documentation, its sibling layers and its source, and found: gpkg_ogr_contents still cached feature counts for 7 dropped exploratory tables; 131,755 empty strings where NULL is the documented convention, which also made the projected copies disagree with their base layer; mineral_localities_utm32n is the EPSG:32632 copy of mineral_localities_refined, not of mineral_localities as its name and docs said (they differ by up to 11.9 km in 117 rows); one locality (number 70) carried a stale host era/period/age (Cenozoic/Quaternary instead of Mesozoic/Cretaceous); towns_geonames stored elevation as text and its only boolean as the text 'True'/'False', and 7,372 of its 45,415 positions are recorded to 2 decimal places or fewer (now exposed as coord_dp); towns, state_capitals and volcanic_plugs stored each point twice and the copies disagreed by up to 0.1 m; geology_era lacked the class_id the other class layers have; three locality layers lacked locality_id; geology_era was documented as reproducing the general-geology sheet's 9 classes when it has 7 era classes and the sheet's are era-plus-lithology. All are fixed (repair_layers.py, normalise_nulls.py) and all are now checks in audit_layers.py. docs_check.py tests every number in LAYERS.md against the file.

The checks are part of the build: audit_layers.py (layers, rasters, registers, attribute conventions, geometry hygiene, sentinels, text hygiene, and every stored measurement against the geometry it describes), docs_check.py (every number in LAYERS.md, and every field name in its field tables, against the file), check_polygon_colour.py (class polygons against their sheets), fix_gpkg_hygiene.py (registers), normalise_nulls.py (NULL convention), describe_layers.py (per-layer descriptions), repair_layers.py (the repairs themselves, idempotent). A release should show 0 problems, 0 wrong claims and 0 empty strings.

A fourth, deeper pass on 2026-10-27 checked things the earlier passes had not: the rings themselves, the text, the sentinel values, and whether each stored measurement is the measurement of the geometry in the row. Fixed: 35 hairline slits (up to 7.1 km, zero width) and 14 duplicate vertices in geology_units, 95 slits in geology_era, plus their copies rebuilt; 42 x -9999 and 2 small negatives in towns_geonames.dem_m (SRTM voids) made NULL; mineral_symbols.link cut at 'colour not consi' in 448 rows and alt-names lists cut mid-name; poly_population class_name '0 - 110,85' completed to '0 - 110,852'; geology_units.formation carried a '(chart key)' provenance tag in 12 rows, a dash before 'Formation', a double space, and three lithologies where a formation name was expected; towns_geonames gave one Nigeria place the neighbouring country's time zone; water_bodies areas were up to 10 km2 from the geometry's own EPSG:6933 area and its in-Nigeria area exceeded its total (frac 1.0006); km_in_nigeria was measured on the equal-area grid while len_km was geodesic, so in-Nigeria length exceeded the whole line in 3,174 rows across six layers - both are geodesic now and frac_in_nigeria is their ratio; international_boundary's length field was called length_km, the only line layer not using len_km. area / length / perimeter conventions are now one per file: area in EPSG:6933, length and perimeter geodesic. One repair was itself defective and is the reason check_idempotency.py exists: towns_geonames.state_agree was converted rather than recomputed, so a second run read the stored 0/1 and turned all 29,470 True values into False while every type and NULL check still passed. It is recomputed from state vs state_gn (29,903 agree, 2,010 do not, 13,502 cannot be compared), and the whole pipeline is now fingerprinted row by row before and after a second run.

A fifth pass on 2026-10-27 looked for the failure modes the earlier passes kept finding: a claim that no longer matched the file, a check that silently stopped checking, and evidence that was current only by accident. Fixed: LAYERS.md said "23 layers in EPSG:4326 (56,947 features)" where the file has 26 / 57,364 - the CRS-split sentence wraps across two lines in the markdown and docs_check.py's pattern used a literal space, so the check had been matching nothing and reporting 0 wrong; the pattern now allows a line break and an unparseable claim is itself a failure (the same guard was added to the header-totals claim). towns_geonames.md gave elevation_m as 45,393 non-NULL rows; that is the number of rows *without* a spot height - GeoNames records one for 22 of the 45,415 places, and dem_m (45,371) is the field to use. "2,638 rows share an exact coordinate" described the repeats; 4,373 rows in all sit on a shared coordinate, and the page now says both. crs_qa_report.json was the record of a 27-layer build and its own guidance line said '+3.66 %' while its measured value was 3.6831 %, so it is now recomputed from the shipped file by refresh_crs_report.py. Added: the provenance and the four source licences are now inside the file (gpkg_metadata + gpkg_metadata_reference, 4 records / 11 references, ISO 19139 XML, written by add_gpkg_metadata.py), so a .gpkg copied on its own still carries the GeoNames CC BY 4.0 attribution and the withdrawn-positions notice; audit_layers.py re-parses them and fails if either goes missing. Added: VERIFICATION.md, generated by verify_all.py, which lists every check, its verdict, and whether that verdict is older than the data - a stale verdict is treated as a failure, which is the defect class that produced the stale prose fixed in this pass. docs_check.py now also checks the numbers in towns_geonames.md and minerals_named.md (442 claims in total, 0 wrong). check_idempotency.py compares every column including fid and now runs add_gpkg_metadata.py as well: the whole pipeline is row-for-row identical on a second run.
